draft.title: Rates and best buys
card: A rate compares two quantities with different units. Speed in km/h and price in $/kg are rates. The word per means for each one.
To find a unit rate, divide the first quantity by the second. 6 kg of apples for $21 costs $21 ÷ 6 = $3.50 per kg.
To compare two deals, find the unit rate of each in the same unit. The deal with the lower price per unit is the better buy.
Unit rates also find totals. At 80 km/h, a car travels 80 × 2.5 = 200 km in 2.5 hours.
draft.remember: Divide to get a rate per one unit, then compare the unit rates.

a.q: A cyclist in Hobart rides 45 km in 3 hours at a steady pace. What is the rate?
a.why: Divide distance by time: 45 ÷ 3 = 15 km/h. Multiplying to get 135 is the tempting mistake, but a rate is found by dividing.

b.q: At a shop in Alice Springs, 5 kg of rice costs $12.50 and 3 kg costs $8.40. Which is the better buy, and why?
opts: 3 kg, because it costs less in total
b.why: 5 kg costs $12.50 ÷ 5 = $2.50 per kg. 3 kg costs $8.40 ÷ 3 = $2.80 per kg. The 5 kg bag has the lower price per kg. The lower total for 3 kg is tempting but it buys less rice.
b.clue: Find the price per kg for both bags.
